omnipotent

om-NIP-uh-tent · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Omnipotent is having unlimited power; able to do anything.

In the myth, the omnipotent sky god could reshape mountains or summon storms with a single thought.

Example

As the company's sole owner and only decision-maker, she was practically omnipotent within the small business, answering to absolutely no one.

Holding total, unlimited power over something, with no real limits or checks, is exactly what omnipotent describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

almighty: Almighty means having complete, unlimited power, and in serious use it is essentially a title reserved for God -- the Almighty. Omnipotent states the same idea as an ordinary description, one writers now apply, often teasingly, to bosses, computers, and committees.

invincible: Invincible means impossible to defeat -- no rival can ever beat you, but your power might stop there. Omnipotent is broader: able to do absolutely anything at all, with no limit on what, not merely safe from every challenger.

supreme: Supreme means highest in rank or authority -- above every rival, the way a supreme court outranks all other courts. Omnipotent is about ability rather than rank: an omnipotent being can do anything at all, not merely sit at the top.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

powerless: lacking any power or ability to act

weak: having little strength or power

Where it sits · how few limits it has

all-powerful → omnipotent

all-powerful vs. omnipotent: All-powerful is lighter than omnipotent: a person holding the only vault key can feel all-powerful for a moment, but omnipotent means truly unlimited power over everything.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — omni-: all (Latin)

root — potent-: power, ability (Latin)

Put it together: Omnipotent combines the Latin prefix omni- ('all') with potens ('having power'), from posse ('to be able'). Something omnipotent literally 'can do all' -- there is no limit to its power.

Use the root in a new word: potential: The realtor kept repeating the word potential as she walked us through the crumbling farmhouse.

Root Check

Word Choice

Omnipotent completes the omni- family alongside omniscient (all-knowing) and omnipresent (everywhere) -- together, the three words describe the three qualities traditionally used to define an all-powerful, all-knowing, ever-present deity, though modern usage happily applies all three more loosely, and often with a wink, to powerful people, systems, or technology.
